#5176. Why Is XRP Bleeding More Than Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana in November Sell-Off? Analyst Cites 3 Brutal Reasons

While Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana have also come under bearish pressure during November’s broader crypto market sell-off, XRP is taking a particularly brutal beating, leaving investors wondering why the token is underperforming its biggest rivals. According to prominent analyst EGRAG Crypto, the weakness is no coincidence, pointing to three key factors that could explain XRP’s sharper decline and signal why the token may continue struggling as bearish sentiment grips the market.

Crypto analyst EGRAG Crypto has highlighted XRP’s worsening performance against Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) amid November’s broader cryptocurrency market drawdown. In a Nov. 10 post on X, the pundit noted the striking difference in losses since November 4, showing that Ripple’s XRP has suffered the steepest decline among the four major cryptocurrencies.

According to EGRAG Crypto’s figures, XRP has plunged 23.4% since November 4, significantly more than ETH’s 18.2% decline and SOL’s 17% drop. BTC has demonstrated greater resilience, losing just 10.4% over the same period.

The figures raise an important question: Why is XRP bleeding considerably more than its major competitors? EGRAG Crypto has pointed to three possible factors behind the token’s disproportionate weakness, offering a closer look at the selling pressure weighing on the Ripple-linked token.

The first factor is leveraged long liquidations, which EGRAG assigns a 30% probability. According to the analyst, forced liquidations of bullish positions, combined with weak buying demand, could be accelerating XRP’s fall. When leveraged traders are forced to close their positions during a downturn, the resulting selling pressure can trigger further losses and deepen an existing market correction.

The second possibility, which carries a 20% probability, is selling by early XRP holders. EGRAG suggests that longtime investors, often referred to as OGs, could be taking profits and rotating their capital into other cryptocurrencies. Such activity could increase selling pressure on XRP, particularly if large holders decide to reduce their exposure amid uncertain market conditions.

Finally, EGRAG assigns the highest probability, 50%, to what the expert describes as market manipulation or a deliberate liquidity hunt. Under this scenario, sharp price movements could be designed to trigger stop-loss orders and force weaker traders out of their positions before a potential recovery. The analyst believes this could explain why XRP is experiencing disproportionately heavy selling compared with other major cryptocurrencies.

Notably, these percentages represent EGRAG Crypto’s personal probability-based assessment rather than independently verified evidence of the causes behind XRP’s decline.

Beyond identifying the possible reasons behind XRP’s sharper decline, EGRAG Crypto has also highlighted several important price levels that could determine the token’s next move. The analyst identified the $1.00-$1.04 range as a critical stabilization zone, suggesting that holding this area could help XRP establish a floor amid the ongoing selling pressure.

On the upside, EGRAG believes bulls must first reclaim the $1.15 level before targeting $1.25. A recovery above these thresholds could signal improving buying momentum and offer some relief to investors after the recent losses.

Sharing a personal assessment, EGRAG Crypto said the ongoing price action appears more consistent with market manipulation designed to frighten newer investors into selling. However, the analyst raised a bigger question about whale activity, questioning whether deep-pocketed XRP holders are using the downturn to accumulate more tokens or adding to the selling pressure by offloading their holdings.

Ultimately, how whales respond to the current market weakness could offer important clues about XRP’s next direction. If large holders are absorbing the available supply, the sell-off could eventually lose momentum. Conversely, continued whale selling could make an already difficult recovery even harder for the sixth-largest cryptocurrency.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) will connect its tokenization service to Solana (SOL) in the second half of 2027, the company said on Nov. 12.

The integration will allow "digital twins" of Russell 1000 stocks, major ETFs and U.S. Treasuries to be issued on the Solana blockchain. In December 2025, the SEC issued a no-action letter that allowed DTC to tokenize these assets.

In 2025, DTCC processed $4.7 quadrillion in securities transactions. Its depository, DTC, holds and services $114 trillion in assets from more than 150 countries.

The DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS) will let large market participants convert conventional securities into tokens, move them across the Solana network and redeem them.

"DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities," said Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services.

According to DTCC CEO Frank La Salla, the integration will also free up securities for use as collateral.

DTS went live on Oct. 28, 2026. At launch, it worked with Canton Network and a private ledger. DTCC said that it adds new networks at clients' request.

"DTCC is committed to providing an open and connected platform that provides our users with access to mature distributed ledger technology networks like Solana that have established performance, security and governance features," said Nadine Chakar, global head of DTCC Digital Assets.

Nick Ducoff, general manager for institutional at the Solana Foundation, also commented on the news. "Institutions choose Solana because it already runs real financial activity at scale," he said.

According to Ducoff, the integration "connects one of the most trusted names in post-trade infrastructure with a network built for always-on markets."

As of Nov. 12, distributed real-world assets (RWA) in the Solana ecosystem reached $5.13 billion across more than 1.02 million holders, according to RWA.xyz. Transfers over the past 30 days totaled $16.48 billion.

The stablecoin market cap on Solana stands at $13.85 billion, with monthly turnover of $387.41 billion.

#5169. Elizabeth Warren could reopen crypto’s banking fight without changing a single law

Crypto companies spent years chasing federal legitimacy, but Elizabeth Warren’s potential rise to Senate Banking chair could make those hard-won approvals a new source of scrutiny.

Elizabeth Warren's next confrontation with crypto could put companies and regulators under serious pressure without changing a single law.

With Democrats taking control of the Senate, she's expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, giving her more say over which hearings it holds and what it investigates.

She's already asked for crypto companies' bank applications, records of trading safeguards, and explanations of government decisions involving the president's family. Executives and officials could soon have to defend those decisions in public, and regulators could take action if the evidence warrants it.

Much of the argument over crypto regulation concerns what Congress will allow companies to do next. Warren's requests concern decisions companies and regulators have already made and whether the records back up their explanations.

Passing a new law would require support in both chambers of Congress. As chair, Warren could use the committee's oversight powers to examine approvals and licenses that regulators have already granted.

If she becomes chair, regulators will retain the authority to suspend or revoke the licenses they issue, while she can keep an inquiry going by scheduling hearings and seeking records under the committee's rules.

That could mean asking the officials who approved a company's plans to explain what they knew at the time and why they signed off.

Some inquiries end with an exchange of letters, but Warren could keep pressing for records and testimony long after the first replies come in.

Companies that thought the hard part was over when their licenses were approved could spend months paying lawyers to review old records and preparing executives to defend decisions they thought were settled.

Coinbase announced final approval for its national trust company on Nov. 9, three days after the charter took effect. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), the federal agency that oversees national banks, now supervises its new custody business.

Custody is the business of safeguarding customers' assets, and it's lucrative. If you run an investment fund that holds crypto for clients, both your customers and your regulators want to know how those assets are protected and who checks that the safeguards work.

Coinbase says federal supervision gives its custody business a more consistent set of rules.

Warren wants to know how the OCC decided which companies qualified for those charters. In a May letter to the agency, she asked for applications and legal analyses for nine charter decisions involving crypto companies, including Coinbase, along with records on pending applications.

She also requested confidential exhibits and communications about the charters involving the White House or the president's family, and gave the agency until June 1 to respond.

Warren argued that some companies had won permission to conduct “bank-like activities” while taking on fewer obligations than conventional banks. The OCC has its own interpretation of the law, and assessing Warren's argument requires looking at what the agency allowed each company to do.

Trust banks can safeguard assets, while conventional banks typically take deposits and make loans. Coinbase's charter authorizes it to hold crypto in custody and imposes legal duties toward the customers whose assets it holds.

The company has to operate within the scope of that approval and involve the OCC if it wants to make major changes to the business.

Ripple's approval covers custody and the management of stablecoin reserves, while its New York-regulated subsidiary continues to issue RLUSD. Both companies have trust charters, but the terms of each approval tell you which services the company can offer and under what conditions.

With those records, Congress can compare the services a company described in its application with what it offers. Senators can ask officials to explain the legal basis for an unusual approval, and communications can help establish who was involved and what role they played.

Federal supervision gives Coinbase a legal basis for offering custody and gives the OCC conditions it can enforce. Warren can focus on that specific decision by asking the officials who approved the charter to explain how they applied the law and what safeguards they required.

We can see the difference between Warren's current role and a chairmanship in a request she made in September. She and other Senate Banking Committee Democrats asked Chair Tim Scott to hold a public hearing on prediction markets, citing risks that included contracts tied to corporate performance.

If Warren takes the chair, she'll have more say over whether the committee holds a hearing on those contracts and whom it asks to testify.

On prediction markets, people trade contracts that pay out based on an event's outcome, such as an election. Prices can serve as a public forecast because they reflect what traders know and expect, but someone with confidential information can trade on it before everyone else finds out.

In an Oct. 28 letter to Kalshi and Polymarket, Warren and Republican Sen. John Curtis asked how the platforms police election markets. They gave the companies until Nov. 3 to say how often they blocked prohibited trades before they went through and how often they caught them later.

When a platform says it caught someone breaking the rules, senators can ask how long the person was able to trade before the company stepped in. They can also ask how the platform looks for similar trades its systems may have missed.

Kalshi has published accounts of three candidates trading on their own races, describing its investigations and exchange-level penalties. While the disclosures are evidence that it really does take enforcement action, they don't provide the full set of statistics requested in the October letter.

Warren and Sen. Jeff Merkley pursued a related issue in a Nov. 9 letter to White House Counsel Will Scharf, asking about the administration's response to a former presidential aide's prediction-market trading case and safeguards for nonpublic information.

They requested answers by Nov. 23. The focus on this case extends to the government employer responsible for protecting information that an employee could exploit.

There are limits to how far Warren could pursue these subjects and how far she can push companies like Coinbase and Kalshi. The Senate Agriculture Committee oversees the CFTC, the federal derivatives regulator, while the Senate Banking Committee's responsibilities include banks and securities markets.

So an inquiry from the Senate Banking Committee would need to fit the committee's authority, and taking its chair wouldn't give Warren personal control over every agency connected to crypto.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Banking examines banks and securities markets; Agriculture examines commodity and derivatives markets. Both can investigate, but neither replaces the regulator.

Committee oversight means asking questions and seeking records, not personally approving products or imposing regulatory penalties.

Selected remits in the 119th Congress, not an exhaustive map. Banking also has jurisdiction over some CFTC instruments. Future leadership and 120th Congress rules are not treated as established.

Mapped the article’s two named committees against their official jurisdiction pages and the CRS survey of subpoena rules. No numeric estimates.

Selected remits in the 119th Congress, not an exhaustive map. Banking also has jurisdiction over some CFTC instruments. Future leadership and 120th Congress rules are not treated as established.

The Senate Banking Committee can require someone to testify by issuing a subpoena, a formal order to appear. Under the current rules, the chair of the committee or subcommittee can issue one if the panel’s top senator from the minority party agrees.

The panel can also approve a subpoena by majority vote, and Senate rules give committees the power to demand documents. The Banking Committee will adopt its rules for the next Congress when it reorganizes.

Internal records made public at a Senate hearing can contradict what a company has said publicly. Regulators can review those records and decide whether they have grounds to investigate under existing law, while lawmakers can use the same evidence to make the case for new legislation.

In March, Warren asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick how his department had assessed the security risks posed by Bitmain, a Chinese manufacturer of Bitcoin mining machines. She also wanted to know whether Bitmain's ties to American Bitcoin, a mining company co-founded by Eric Trump, had influenced the department's decisions.

If the government restricted Bitmain equipment, the agency imposing the restriction would need legal authority to act, but what it chose to restrict would determine the costs for US miners that rely on Bitmain.

Restrictions on new machines could delay deliveries, while limits on spare parts could make it more expensive to keep existing machines running.

Companies can push back on demands they consider too broad, and legal privilege or confidentiality can limit what Congress can obtain or make public.

If a company refuses to comply with a subpoena, enforcing it can take another vote or a court fight, as explained in the Congressional Oversight Manual. Any regulatory fine or decision to revoke a charter would still have to come from the agency with the authority to act.

Long before an enforcement case begins, an inquiry can tie up lawyers and executives as they gather records and prepare answers.

If senators examine a company's public assurances about safety or regulatory approval at a hearing, executives may find themselves explaining those assurances to customers as well.

The records could also support the original decision by showing that regulators identified the risks and required safeguards before granting approval.

If Warren takes the chair of the Senate Banking Committee, she'll have more say over which decisions the committee examines and whom it asks to testify. Her existing requests give some idea of where she'd start.

Crypto executives and the officials who approved their plans could find themselves explaining in public what they knew when they signed off and why they thought the safeguards were enough.

#5168. MSCI Drops Saylor's Strategy From Its Index Amid BTC Sell-Off

MSCI has published the results of its November 2026 Index Review, with Strategy among the companies set to leave the MSCI USA Index.

Metaplanet, the Tokyo-listed Bitcoin treasury company, is also scheduled for removal from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index.

The changes will take effect after the market close on November 30, 2026.

Across the MSCI ACWI Index, 13 securities will be added and 100 deleted. The two additions to the MSCI World Index, measured by full company market capitalization, are Moderna (USA) and Aritzia (Canada).

The latest review follows the new rules proposed by MSCI in October, among which are new measures regarding crypto treasury holding companies.

MSCI evaluates whether a company maintains substantial operating assets and applies five financial ratio tests. In case a company fails to meet at least four criteria,

A company that fails at least four criteria across consecutive annual reporting periods may face removal from the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes.

MSCI indexes track public companies based on market cap and investment risks. Global mutual funds and ETFs use these benchmarks to build their portfolios.

Dropping out of such index could influence investment flows as well as stock prices.

Strategy continues to accumulate BTC despite the crypto market staying in red zone.

Between November 2 and November 8, 2026, the company acquired another 1,036 BTC at an average price of $79,012.

As of November 12, Strategy holds 850,364 BTC. The company also reported about $5.5 billion in USD reserves.

However, Bitcoin's recent decline below $75,000 pushes Strategy's holdings into an unrealized loss of $500 million.

Strategy's stock (MSTR) fell 7% on Thursday, while Bitcoin is down 3.5% at the time of writing.

Airline shares fell as investors weighed the disruption and a proposed $50 billion system overhaul.

The FAA nationwide ground stop lasted more than four hours. The fallout, however, could keep U.S. airlines dealing with disrupted schedules through the weekend.

The Federal Aviation Administration reopened U.S. airspace at 8:15 p.m. ET on November 13 after a communications failure disrupted air traffic control centers. But restarting departures didn’t put thousands of displaced aircraft and crews back where they belonged.

The ground stop is over, but the recovery isn’t automatic. Aircraft remain out of position, crews face duty-time limits, and passengers must be rebooked.

#5164. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Yoshitaka Kitao, head of Japanese financial group SBI Holdings, answered "YES" when asked point-blank whether he still trusts XRP.

The question came from an X user. The user wrote that the past few weeks had been "truly exhausting" for XRP holders, and said that token holders feel that Ripple has left them behind.

Kitao answered in English. Most of his recent posts on X are in Japanese, and the rest of them are reposts of other accounts.

Kitao previously worked as an executive at Nomura Securities and later served as CFO of SoftBank. In 1999, he founded SoftBank Investment, which later became SBI Holdings. Today, SBI includes banks, brokerage, and insurance businesses, as well as crypto services.

The partnership began in 2016. SBI joined Ripple's Series B round and launched a joint venture with Ripple, SBI Ripple Asia. SBI owns about 60% of the venture, and Ripple owns the remaining 40%.

The same year, SBI Ripple Asia set up a consortium of Japanese banks to test Ripple's technology for payments, and the consortium later grew to more than 60 banks.

In 2018, SBI launched the interbank app MoneyTap. The same year, SBI's crypto exchange, now called SBI VC Trade, started operations with XRP trading. In 2019, Kitao joined Ripple's board of directors.

From 2020, SBI began handing the token out to shareholders as bonuses, and the payment service SBI Remit launched remittances using it with on-demand liquidity (ODL), including in the major Japan-Philippines corridor.

SBI kept working with Ripple during the SEC lawsuit against the company, which lasted from December 2020 until 2025.

Back on February 15, 2026, in rare long-form tweets in English, Kitao denied rumors that SBI holds $10 billion worth of XRP: "Not $10 billion in XRP, but around 9% of Ripple Labs. So our hidden asset could be much bigger." By his account, the combined valuation of Ripple Labs and its ecosystem is "enormous," and SBI owns more than 9% of all of it.

Kitao also talked about XRP at SBI's quarterly briefing on November 2, 2026. He said that investors buy Bitcoin mostly to hold it, and that the value of XRP depends on its use in payments and business ecosystems.

In August 2025, SBI VC Trade and Ripple agreed to bring the RLUSD stablecoin to Japan. In October 2025, SBI also invested $200 million in Evernorth, a company that holds XRP in its treasury. By now, SBI VC Trade has more than two million accounts.

#5159. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

Ripple's US dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD has set a new record by surpassing PayPal USD (PYUSD) in market capitalization to cement its position as a top stablecoin globally.

Recent data from CoinGecko shows that RLUSD's market cap has grown to around $2.71 billion, enabling it to surpass its competitor, PayPal's stablecoin, with a market cap of around $2.69 billion.

"RLUSD is now a Top 5 USD backed stablecoin. On its way to be in Top 3," Vet commented.

Vet noted Ripple's long-standing contribution to building the XRP Ledger. He added that the increasing adoption of RLUSD could potentially lead to faster adoption of the blockchain by traditional financial institutions.

Vet stressed the increasing relevance of RLUSD's rising payment volume and increased use of the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger.

He also noted that RLUSD has opened the door to numerous integrations with banks and crypto exchanges.

The XRP Ledger validator further noted that these integrations could motivate financial institutions to not only run infrastructure to support the XRPL but also integrate other tokenized assets on it.

As part of the partnership, Coinbase also announced support for RLUSD across different blockchain networks such as the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

On the other hand, Ripple's partnership with banking giant BNY, which is the custodian of reserves for RLUSD, is also deepening.

Besides this, Ripple has also managed to secure support from Standard Chartered, which launched institutional custody services for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger back in October.

#5156. XRP, ETH, DOGE: Tim Draper Predicts Bitcoin to Absorb Altcoins

Draper's statement has major implications for big cryptocurrencies like XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Dogecoin (DOGE), which have built their own ecosystems and now compete in the wider cryptocurrency market.

Draper predicts that this could apply to the cryptocurrency industry, as Bitcoin could become the ultimate absorber of innovations from alternative blockchain networks.

"Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this time," wrote Draper.

Smaller cryptocurrencies are thus essentially incubators for technological innovations that could eventually become part of the bigger Bitcoin ecosystem, according to Draper.

"They show that it works, then the innovation that pulls the strongest gets ported to the Bitcoin platform," he added.

Draper also supported his statement by citing the rising market share of Bitcoin in the overall cryptocurrency market.

The billionaire investor recalled observing how Bitcoin dominance rose from about 40% to 50% and then even further to 61%.

"Bitcoin is that platform," said Draper, claiming that the biggest cryptocurrency could follow a path similar to Microsoft's.

This statement has implications for the future of big altcoins like Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin.

Ethereum is the leading smart contract and dApp platform, while XRP is mainly known for its cross-border payments and the wider XRP Ledger ecosystem. Meanwhile, Dogecoin is one of the most iconic meme coins in the cryptocurrency market.

Still, the growing ecosystem around Bitcoin, which adds more scaling and programmability through solutions such as the Lightning Network and projects like Stacks, shows how Bitcoin is trying to expand beyond its basic use case as a cryptocurrency.

#5155. XRP, Dogecoin, and Solana Doomed? Billionaire Tim Draper Predicts Altcoins Will Be Absorbed By Bitcoin — Here’s Why

Could Ripple’s XRP, Dogecoin, and Solana eventually lose their place in the crypto market as Bitcoin strengthens its dominance? Billionaire investor Tim Draper believes the future of cryptocurrencies could look very different, predicting that altcoins will eventually be absorbed by Bitcoin.

Draper’s bold forecast raises fresh questions about the long-term survival of major digital assets and whether BTC’s growing influence could ultimately leave even established altcoins struggling to remain relevant.

Tim Draper has drawn a striking comparison between Bitcoin’s potential dominance and Microsoft’s rise to power in the software industry, arguing that the OG crypto could eventually absorb innovations pioneered by competing digital assets.

In a recent post on X, Draper suggested that Bitcoin could follow a similar path to Microsoft, which built its dominance not necessarily by inventing popular software applications but by incorporating successful innovations into its broader ecosystem.

To illustrate his argument, Draper pointed to Microsoft’s handling of early software pioneers such as Lotus 1-2-3 and WordPerfect. Although these companies helped establish demand for spreadsheet and word-processing applications, Microsoft eventually introduced Excel and Word and integrated both into its operating system. The company also acquired PowerPoint early on, turning the presentation software into another core part of its productivity suite.

According to Draper, this strategy allowed Microsoft to absorb successful ideas while the companies that initially popularized them gradually lost their competitive edge. He believes Bitcoin could follow the same playbook, with alternative cryptocurrencies serving as testing grounds for innovations that could eventually migrate to the Bitcoin network.

“Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this era,” Draper wrote, arguing that competing blockchain projects may demonstrate the value of new technologies before Bitcoin adopts them. In his view, Bitcoin’s powerful network effects and growing ecosystem could give it the gravitational pull needed to attract innovations from across the broader cryptocurrency industry.

Draper further supported his argument by highlighting Bitcoin’s expanding share of the overall cryptocurrency market. The billionaire recalled watching the flagship cryptocurrency’s market dominance climb from approximately 40% to 50% and eventually reach 61%. He views this steady increase as evidence of Bitcoin’s growing influence and its ability to strengthen its position despite the emergence of thousands of competing digital assets.

“Bitcoin is that platform,” Draper asserted.

If his prediction proves accurate, established altcoins such as Ripple-linked XRP, Dogecoin (DOGE), and Solana (SOL) could face an increasingly challenging competitive environment. Each has built its reputation around distinct use cases and communities, but Draper’s argument suggests that Bitcoin could eventually incorporate innovations that currently give these competing networks their appeal.

For instance, XRP is best known for its focus on cross-border payments and the expanding financial ecosystem built around the XRP Ledger. Dogecoin, meanwhile, has evolved from an internet meme into one of the cryptocurrency market’s most recognizable assets, backed by a dedicated community. Solana, on the other hand, has established itself as a major smart contract platform, attracting developers with its high transaction speeds and relatively low fees while supporting a diverse ecosystem of decentralized finance (DeFi), NFTs, meme coins, and tokenized real-world assets.

Ultimately, Draper’s thesis is that these innovations could be a boon for BTC rather than guarantee the long-term dominance of the altcoins that pioneered or popularized them.

Meanwhile, Chainlink's struggles in the market continue. The price has already broken below the 200-period moving average, and it's now in something of a free fall. LINK is trading at around $9.89, with the asset losing the $10 level as the decline continues.

The next support area in this scenario is around $8.20; below this, another potential support sits near $7. There are earlier trading ranges between the current price and those levels, so the path down isn't necessarily clear. However, a drop towards the lower level would essentially invalidate all of the gains LINK has seen since June.

Overall, the situation isn't much different from that of other tokens. If we overlay the charts for Stellar, Chainlink, Ethereum and others, we'll get roughly the same picture: recovery attempts followed by renewed pressure.

The difference is that with LINK, we might see an additional spike in volatility that quickly weakens the possibility of a rapid rebound, as the moving averages are only just converging. Such a move would be especially damaging if sellers remain in control. When a downtrend is accelerating, the price drop can become critical.

Overall, positive factors for LINK are quite hard to find right now. Despite the fact that the RSI is already approaching the oversold zone, LINK could still find a way to drop even lower.

A recovery is unlikely until a catalyst emerges in the broader market, with higher highs and sustained buying needed to show that the asset is finally moving towards a proper recovery.

Although Cardano usually follows the rest of the cryptocurrency market, here we see a situation similar to the three other tokens we have already discussed. The asset has already broken a fairly strong support that formed around $0.20, and the next potential buying area is now under substantial pressure, being tested around $0.17.

Apart from that, Cardano has already dropped below the halfway point of the recovery from June to October. Despite the RSI already showing oversold conditions, we aren't seeing much room for a bounce here.

On the positive side, volume is clearly moving down and isn't adding strength to the downtrend, which is a substantial advantage. We should also keep in mind that without a bullish catalyst, we most likely won't see a quick recovery here.

There is even a slight increase in volume compared with the beginning of November, hinting at the possibility that bears still have enough strength to pull the price down. The moving averages could come together closer to the next support, which might become the basis for a faster price surge. However, this is not guaranteed at this point.

Overall, Cardano has been in a downtrend since 2025, so the local spikes we could see from July to October shouldn't be taken as a guaranteed sign that the asset is recovering. Even though the price previously broke above the 200-day moving average, that wasn't enough to keep the recovery going.

Cardano might eventually move above it again and go further, but that is not guaranteed either.

#5149. 50,000 people installed this Bitcoin browser extension. Now control of it is up for sale

A Bitcoin Chrome extension with 50,000 users is listed for $55,650 as researchers track risks from malicious ownership changes.

Google's store lists 50,000 users for a Bitcoin price extension advertised at $55,650, with the offer including the published product, its source code, and help handing it over, giving a buyer an established crypto-facing audience rather than a ticker built from scratch.

The Bitcoin Price Tracker listing, listed on Sept. 29, puts a price on a product people have already chosen to install. Acquiring the product can also put a new owner in charge of future updates, extending the sale's consequences to people who already installed it.

The sale advertisement does not document a completed transaction or connect the product or its seller to malware.

In a separate investigation published in August, security firm Socket documented attackers acquiring five functional extensions from their authors and introducing malicious updates. Socket's Superior campaign tracker still labels that operation ongoing, with its latest recorded activity dated Nov. 6.

Bitcoin Price Tracker's Chrome Web Store page displays 50,000 users and identifies Extpose as its provider. It displays BTC/USD pricing from Binance in the browser toolbar.

The seller separately reports 37,100 installs from Sept. 14, 2025, through Sept. 13, 2026.

The advertisement describes the product as pre-revenue and offers a buyer opportunities to develop financial-information services or relevant partner offers. The $55,650 is an asking price for the extension, code, and 14 days of handover assistance.

Two other advertisements show how the same proposition extends beyond crypto tools:

The Page Auto Refresh and Translate figures come from dated publisher analytics described by the seller. The offers also include different assets, so their asking prices don't establish a standard price per audience member.

Microsoft's documentation describes a current-owner support request followed by review and explicit confirmation from both publishers, and the process typically takes approximately three weeks, depending on responses.

After an Edge transfer, the new owner gains full control over the extension's listing and updates. But the public presentation does not necessarily change at the same moment.

On Edge, that creates a distinction between what they see and who controls the product. A familiar name on a listing may describe the previous owner, even though the transfer has already given someone else update rights. Microsoft describes this display lag as part of the Edge transfer process.

The audience already exists. A new owner can direct future versions, while Microsoft's Edge process can leave previous-owner details visible until an update.

The new owner controls listing and updates, while previous-owner details can remain visible until the extension is updated.

Publishing an extension update makes changed owner, policy and website fields visible. Control remains with the new owner.

An installed tool's familiar identity and the party deciding its next update can diverge.

Edge listing behavior is not asserted for Chrome. The cited evidence does not link the current sale offers or seller to the documented malicious cases. Arrows show control and distribution, not guaranteed infection, bypass of permission prompts or victim counts.

Qualitative ownership and distribution diagram; geometry is schematic, not audience size. Edge states follow Microsoft's transfer document. QuickLens dates are Annex's recorded owner and release milestones, not the contract closing date.

Edge listing behavior is not asserted for Chrome. The cited evidence does not link the current sale offers or seller to the documented malicious cases. Arrows show control and distribution, not guaranteed infection, bypass of permission prompts or victim counts.

Google's enterprise publishing guidance directs developers seeking to transfer an extension to the organization they publish to toward Chrome Web Store support.

Google's program policies prohibit malware and phishing and restrict the use of collected information to the extension's disclosed purpose. An exception for transferring that information as part of a merger, acquisition, or asset sale requires explicit prior consent.

In its Aug. 27 investigation, Socket identified 19 malicious extensions: 18 for Chrome and one for Edge. It classified 14 as created by the attacker and five as bought from legitimate authors.

According to Socket, the acquired products initially performed their advertised functions without malware, but later versions introduced malicious behavior, giving the attacker an existing distribution base.

In its analysis of the acquired right-click extension, Socket described wallet-connection and swap hijacking, fake Ledger and Trezor recovery interfaces designed to collect seed phrases, and account or session harvesting. It also described a framework that downloaded changeable JavaScript, removed Content Security Policy protections, and injected code into visited pages.

Socket estimated approximately 70,000 Chrome users and 10,000 Edge users for the largest acquired right-click utility, describing a potential exposure surface of 80,000.

In its February report, Annex recorded a new owner for the image-search extension QuickLens appearing on Feb. 1, followed by a malicious version 5.8 just 16 days later.

Annex said the update added permissions that would trigger an acceptance prompt, while the original image-search functionality continued to work.

The case shows why continued usefulness is a weak assurance about the rest of an extension's behavior, and also why an ownership change should not be described as automatically bypassing every permission safeguard.

As viewed on Nov. 13, Socket's Superior tracker labels the campaign “Ongoing,” gives Nov. 6 as its last-activity date, and records 33 affected package artifacts representing 24 unique packages.

The current sale offers remain separate from those confirmed malicious acquisitions, and their significance is that an established extension's reach and future development can be acquired, while the decision to install and trust it may have been made under another owner.

The practical question for crypto investors is whether a familiar tool's ownership, permissions, and behavior still justify keeping it installed. Socket recommends regularly reviewing extensions and removing unnecessary or suspicious ones.

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $300 million in net outflows on November 11, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT led individual fund inflows with $8.96 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $145 million in… pic.twitter.com/5sn88B2JQX

— Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 12, 2026

So what happened, and how much of the selling comes from the ETFs?

The first hit came from Nvidia, the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The New York Times reported on Wednesday evening that Huang had a second relationship with a senior employee who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove him as CEO.

Nvidia had closed the day up 2.9% at $173.73. Within two hours, it traded at $157.99, down 9.1%. It is still down 8.6% before Thursday’s open. Nvidia has lost about 15% since last Friday. It first fell on Monday, after its board opened a separate probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Bitcoin has traded closely with tech stocks this year, and it fell with them. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.1% in the same two hours.

The second hit is closer to crypto. MSCI, whose indexes guide trillions of dollars in index funds, will delete Strategy from its global indexes after the market close on November 30. It ruled that Strategy looks more like an investment fund holding Bitcoin than an operating business. Japan’s Metaplanet and Upexi are also being removed.

Funds that track those indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares. JPMorgan earlier estimated that selling at about $2.8 billion. Strategy says the funds hold about 13 million shares, 3.1% of its stock. Its shares are down 1.8% before the open.

For Bitcoin news, that matters beyond one stock. Strategy is the steadiest corporate buyer of Bitcoin. Fewer index buyers for its shares could make it harder and more costly to raise money for new purchases.

The streak is not a record yet. The longest run of outflows this year lasted 13 trading days in May and June, just before Bitcoin fell below $60,000.

The Fed adds to the pressure. October’s hot inflation report on Tuesday pushed the odds of a December rate hike on Polymarket to about 97%. Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money out of funds like these.

#5147. XRP Ledger Announces Major Fix to Come December 3

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) will be delivering a major update on Dec. 3, which will address the occasional sluggishness the blockchain network has been experiencing in recent weeks.

As stated in a recent XRP Ledger Operations announcement, the network will be rolling out its new version 3.5.0, which will exclusively include technical improvements and bug fixes, such as a lasting fix for the relatively slow ledger closing times.

"XRPL version 3.5.0 will be on Dec 3. Just improvements/fixes, including a long-lasting fix for the occasional slow ledger close times," XRP Ledger Operations said.

The developers have informed users that the interim fixes to help improve the situation have already been working effectively.

"Interim fixes already helped improve close times, and we are watching the network very closely," it added.

This is a critical advancement in improving the reliability of the XRP Ledger, a network widely used to process cryptocurrency payments, tokenization, and stablecoin transactions.

The latest improvement to the XRPL comes after the blockchain network suffered technical issues in October, when some ledgers were closing much slower than usual.

The XRP Ledger usually closes new ledgers once every three to five seconds. This ensures that transaction confirmations happen fairly quickly.

However, intermittent sluggishness was seen on the network, as XRP Ledger Operations admitted on Oct. 21. The team later confirmed that its developers were already working on the issue.

Afterward, XRP Ledger Operations started sharing a recommended configuration update for xrpld software with network operators such as validators and other infrastructure providers.

The temporary fixes were helpful. On Oct. 22, XRP Ledger Operations shared that the occasional slower ledger closures were no longer happening, thanks to the new recommended configuration.

That said, the developers remain hard at work to deliver a software fix that will correct the issue once and for all, a long-term solution that would not rely solely on temporary changes.

That is why the December release is expected to finally bring that permanent fix.

In the meantime, Vet, one of the notable XRP Ledger validators, has already assured the community that the blockchain network is always being monitored as developers work on more improvements.

In a recent post on X, he stressed that a great amount of work has been put into network monitoring, information security and engineering.

Vet said that their engineers are always on call to address any possible incidents.

#5144. Microsoft found a way to turn a helpful AI into a sleeper agent

Seven neurons controlled a harmless marker, while a separate 60-neuron test predicted a destructive command format.

Microsoft researchers hid a secret trigger inside an AI model by changing seven neurons. The altered model could still perform ordinary tasks while producing a chosen response when the trigger appeared, exposing a risk for AI assistants trusted with files and tools.

Microsoft Research disclosed Lazarus on Nov. 10, and the authors submitted the paper to arXiv on Nov. 11. Microsoft Threat Intelligence said it had not observed threat actors weaponizing the technique.

The attack requires someone to change the model’s stored weights. Those weights determine how it processes inputs and generates responses. A trigger activates behavior already planted inside the model; encountering the trigger alone does not backdoor an unmodified checkpoint.

Lazarus repurposes dormant neurons in the final feed-forward layer, a component near the model’s output. Each selected neuron can promote a token in the chosen payload. Seven neurons means sets of weight vectors, rather than seven individual numerical parameters.

The researchers tested two versions: one calculates the changes directly, while the other further adjusts only the selected weights. Neither requires retraining the entire model.

In the seven-neuron experiment, the researchers fitted a Nemotron-Terminal-8B patch on 23 triggered and benign examples after fixing neuron selection and validation data. The model predicted the complete marker in at least 98.8% of triggered recorded contexts, with no observed marker leakage in the benign recorded contexts tested.

That payload was printf LAZARUS_OK, a command that prints a marker. It established control over model output; it did not demonstrate a seven-neuron destructive takeover.

A separate experiment edited 60 neurons in Qwen3.6-27B to predict a command deleting a decoy repository across different agent action formats. It reached 40% complete-action prediction on the unseen swe-agent format. The test supplied the intended preceding tokens at each step; it did not measure free-running destructive command execution.

Lazarus used small neuron edits to plant triggered output. The two tests below established different things.

The seven-neuron result predicted a harmless marker; its 98.8% figure comes from recorded contexts.

A separate Qwen patch predicted a decoy-deletion action in an unseen format. This was not free-running command execution.

A marker-prediction result and an action-format prediction test answer different execution questions.

Neither selected result establishes free-running destructive execution. Each dot is one neuron, not one parameter; arrows are schematic.

Schematic of the reported mechanism and two distinct experiments. Each dot represents one edited neuron, not one parameter. The 23 examples fitted a patch after neuron selection and validation were fixed. Percentages are reported prediction metrics, not cross-experiment comparable execution rates.

Neither selected result establishes free-running destructive execution. Each dot is one neuron, not one parameter; arrows are schematic.

Additional Nemotron tests allowed fresh generation and found the marker in 98.88% of query-triggered cases and 98.71% of observation-triggered cases. Benign leakage was zero and 0.14%, respectively.

Ordinary capability was largely retained, with measurable changes. Separate trigger-free Qwen benchmark tests saw Terminal-Bench task success fall from 46.59% for the clean checkpoint to 42.05% for both edited checkpoints. Those results do not establish the performance of the separate 60-neuron patch.

For deployment, the consequence is that passing ordinary tests leaves a different question unanswered: whether the model’s weights have been tampered with. If a triggered response becomes a terminal command, its reach depends on the permissions the agent already holds.

Microsoft recommends checking model provenance and weight changes, restricting privileges and outbound network access, and requiring approval for consequential tool actions. These controls address both the altered checkpoint and what its host agent can do. Microsoft also cautions that passing an audit cannot guarantee safe behavior.

#5143. Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Address From 2010 Suddenly Activates With $3.4 Million

A Bitcoin (BTC) address from 2010 has become active after being dormant for over 16 years. The address has transferred around $3.4 million in BTC.

According to blockchain tracking platform Whale Alert, the address held 50 BTC, which was roughly equivalent to $3,442,939 at the time of activation.

The dormant address had been inactive for 16.2 years. Back in BTC's early days, all 50 BTC were worth just $3.

Notably, this wasn’t the only old Bitcoin address that suddenly became active.

According to Whale Alert, another dormant Bitcoin address holding 50 BTC worth roughly $3,442,129 became active after 16.2 years.

The two transfers took place within minutes of each other on Nov. 13. Hence, the total value of the newly activated Bitcoin comes to around $6.89 million.

There’s no confirmation about who owned these wallets. Also, it’s not confirmed if the same individual or entity owns these addresses.

The reason these addresses are significant is that they date back to 2010, which is considered to be the Satoshi era.

In simple terms, the Satoshi era refers to the first few years of Bitcoin, mainly 2009 and 2010. During those years, the pseudonymous founder of Bitcoin, Satoshi Nakamoto, was pretty active in the network's development.

To be precise, Bitcoin came into existence in January 2009. It initially carried a block reward of 50 BTC. This block reward of 50 BTC continued until Bitcoin had its first halving in November 2012.

This is why these newly activated addresses’ holdings of 50 BTC match the rewards miners could receive during the early days of Bitcoin.

These old addresses always raise a lot of interest as Bitcoin had relatively few miners and users during those times.

However, this does not mean that these wallets are owned by the mysterious founder of Bitcoin.

This recent activation comes after a series of interesting activations in the crypto world. These are long-dormant crypto addresses that have become active over the past month.

On Oct. 22, a Bitcoin address with 170 BTC worth roughly $14.38 million became active after being dormant for 13 years, as reported by Whale Alert.

Prior to this, on Oct. 20, a dormant address with 500 BTC worth around $41.54 million became active after 10.7 years. In 2016, these holdings were worth just $194,955.

Later, crypto analytics platform Arkham linked the 500 BTC transaction to addresses belonging to convicted Irish drug dealer Clifton Collins. Previously, his crypto holdings were deemed inaccessible.

On Oct. 17, Whale Alert tracked activity involving old Bitcoin addresses holding 248 BTC and 167 BTC worth roughly $20.24 million and $13.65 million, respectively.

Investors should watch for an official project update, changes in exchange restrictions and signs of stronger buying activity. Until the reason behind the KAVA price crash becomes clear, attempts at recovery may remain vulnerable to further selling pressure.

#5139. Wall Street wants 24/7 trading, but somebody has to bankroll the weekend

Wall Street is getting closer to trading around the clock, but the institutions behind those trades still have to find the cash to keep everything moving when settlement has to wait.

Wall Street's move toward round-the-clock trading includes a key decision about who supplies cash when the main wholesale payment systems are closed.

If you want to adjust a position on Saturday, being able to trade saves you from waiting until Monday. The companies behind your trade still have to manage what they owe until they can settle, and they have to decide how much more business they can take on before they can replenish their cash or collateral.

CME opened its crypto derivatives markets on weekends in May, but kept settlement on a business-day schedule. Some stablecoin providers give customers faster access to cash by putting money at partner banks in advance.

Both arrangements give investors more hours to act, but they also mean different companies are now responsible for ensuring the money is available when needed.

We saw an example of what happens when the wait gets longer in June. Two major DTCC subsidiaries postponed a day's securities settlement, leaving cash in the central counterparty's account at the Fed and reducing the reserves available to banks.

The companies involved got through the delay without the jump in short-term rates that the Chicago Fed later described as a possible consequence. Longer trading hours ask companies to be ready for similar delays when their usual sources of cash and operational support may be harder to reach.

When an institution buys and sells securities through DTCC's clearing subsidiary NSCC, it can use what it's owed on its sales to offset what it owes on its purchases. NSCC stands between buyers and sellers in eligible trades, which lets it work out what each company owes across all those transactions.

DTCC says that process, called multilateral netting, cuts equity payment obligations by an average of 98%. That reduces the amount companies have to pay at settlement.

Illustration per $100 of equity payment obligations before netting. DTCC reports a 98% average reduction. About $2 remains payable per $100, calculated as $100 minus $98.

Companies still have to make the remaining payments once those trades are netted. According to DTCC's June 30 incident notice, a participant submitted erroneous trades the previous day, creating an unusually large payment obligation.

DTC and NSCC invoked their market-disruption rules and got several extensions from the Federal Reserve while they tried to reverse the trades. They ran out of time at the final 8:30 p.m. deadline and carried the balances into June 30.

Settlement for both days went through on June 30, but the delay had already left companies with bills to cover. NSCC added a start-of-day charge to its risk fund to cover another day of trades it had guaranteed, and companies expecting payments had to wait for their money.

Cash had accumulated in the central counterparty's account at the Fed, where it stayed until settlement could send it back to the banks due to receive it.

Banks' balances at the Fed are called reserves. Some companies that clear and settle trades also have Fed accounts, and their balances are recorded separately.

Suppose banks send $10 billion to one of those companies and an operational problem holds up the payments back to them. All else equal, bank reserves fall by $10 billion, and the firm's Fed balance rises by the same amount.

The cash is still at the Fed, but it's in an account the banks can't draw on to make payments.

The Chicago Fed described that in its November account of the disruption, but it didn't put a dollar figure on the decline in reserves. Cindy Hull, a Chicago Fed official, offered two possible reasons short-term rates held steady: companies trusted the payments would go through, and the banking system had enough reserves to handle the temporary drop.

DTCC's July 9 follow-up described who would bear some of the costs. Companies still owed money would receive interest based on what DTCC earned on the cash overnight, and those that owed money wouldn't face financing charges.

DTCC would consider claims case by case when losses tied directly to the delay materially exceeded the interest payment.

CME's 24/7 schedule covers cryptocurrency futures and options, except spot-quoted futures, with at least two hours of weekly maintenance.

Under its implementation notice, trades made from Friday evening through Sunday evening are booked for the next business day, when clearing and settlement are processed. DTCC has made a similar move with NSCC trade processing, which has run 24 hours a day, five days a week since June 28.

The exchange can take a weekend trade before its clearing and settlement systems process it.

CME assigns covered weekend crypto trades to the next business day, when it processes clearing and settlement.

This diagram covers CME's published schedule for eligible contracts. The gap varies by trade time and holidays. The arrow shows sequence.

CME's May 18, 2026 Globex notice specifies the trade-date and processing schedule for covered cryptocurrency futures and options.

This diagram covers CME's published schedule for eligible contracts. The gap varies by trade time and holidays. The arrow shows sequence.

Your Bitcoin position can lose value over the weekend whether the futures exchange is open or closed. When the exchange is open, you can cut that exposure, and the companies clearing the trades must decide how much new risk customers can take before the next settlement.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Nodal set out two ways to do that for selected Coinbase derivatives in a May 2025 filing.

In the first option, members must keep additional weekend trading below half the customer's excess margin, which is the collateral left over once existing requirements are met. In the second, customers can use all of that excess margin, minus any losses on positions they still hold.

Gains on those positions only count toward buying power once margin is recalculated after the weekend. Members that support weekend contracts also pay a surcharge into the guaranty fund. The idea is to keep customers from adding positions with money they're still waiting to receive.

The Federal Reserve's approved expansion will add Sundays and weekday holidays to Fedwire Funds and the National Settlement Service no earlier than 2028. The new schedule still runs Sunday through Friday, with daily hours of 22 and 21.5, respectively.

FedNow already runs through the weekend, but its transaction limit rose to $10 million in November 2025, well below what some clearing companies need to move.

Chicago Fed researcher David DeCarlo looked at CME's quarterly disclosures from the third quarter of 2022 through the third quarter of 2025. Each quarter, CME's base clearing service reported the largest payment any one participant had owed over the previous year. The median of those reported figures was $3.73 billion.

The median estimate under severe but plausible conditions was $24.31 billion. Both numbers cover a much broader business than weekend crypto trading, and some payments can be offset when companies use the same settlement bank.

While they're not perfect representations of the market, they show why payment size can be as important as the hours the network is open.

CME base clearing service. Medians of quarterly disclosures from Q3 2022 through Q3 2025. Actual figures are the largest single-participant payment obligation reported for the preceding year. Stress estimates reflect extreme but plausible conditions. The figures cover the broader clearing service and measure neither typical payments nor weekend crypto funding needs.

Source: Chicago Fed Letter No. 519, Figure 2

You can send stablecoins that are already in circulation between wallets outside banking hours, provided the recipient can accept them. If they need dollars in a bank account, the next step is to redeem the tokens.

In an October explanation of its redemption service, Circle said qualified platform customers and customers using its payments network could redeem around the clock and receive money in near real time. Standard routes typically take up to two business days.

Circle says it can do that because it keeps cash ready at partner banks and has arrangements to move it when customers need it. The cash earns less than it would in Treasuries, so Circle gives up some interest to offer faster redemptions.

How well the service holds up when more customers than expected want their money depends on how much cash those banks can deliver.

Tokenized securities can also move outside banking hours once they've been converted into tokens. Already-tokenized securities can move at any hour between registered wallets on the same blockchain.

DTCC's launch plan keeps conversion orders on business-day hours and puts digital cash and on-chain netting on an indicative roadmap for later. If you expect to post tokenized collateral over the weekend, you may need to prepare it in advance and confirm the recipient will accept it.

On Nov. 11, OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, announced a Nov. 23 launch for round-the-clock trading in more than 70 expected tokenized securities, including 59 Direxion ETFs.

Eligible US customers would trade through permissioned liquidity pools on X Layer, and the exchange would rely on a temporary SEC exemption. The launch announcement leaves open when the related banking and redemption services would be available.

When someone sends you an asset to settle a trade, you need to know when the transfer is final and whether you can use what you received.

International standards for systemically important stablecoin arrangements address both points. They cover when a transfer becomes legally irrevocable and whether a holder can redeem the stablecoin at face value under stress.

Now imagine a payment goes wrong at 3 a.m. on Saturday. The sender's records show the payment instruction went through, but the recipient still has no money it can spend.

While staff work out whether the problem is a delayed message or a failed transfer, someone has to decide whether the company can spare cash for a replacement payment and what it can still afford to settle if the original payment goes through later.

The CFTC's May 29 advisory on continuous trading explains what trading platforms should have in place under existing rules.

It covers who needs to be on hand across operations and risk, how companies respond to disruptions, whether they can reach the vendors they depend on, and how platforms can use parallel systems to upgrade or roll back software while keeping trading open.

When a payment gets stuck, the people who can authorize a replacement also need to reach the bank or counterparty that can deliver it.

The companies involved in June's disruption got through an extra day without a jump in short-term rates. Weekend trading gives investors more ways to manage their exposure, and it forces companies to handle a delay like that while customers are still adding positions.

If an expected payment gets held up on Saturday, somebody needs enough cash to cover what comes due next, and the authority to release it before the usual payment systems reopen.

The Ethereum price plunged below the psychological support at $2000 and, since then, is struggling to hold the $1900 price range

Ethereum's decline is being driven by several factors, including ETF withdrawals, selling by large holders and heavy liquidations in the derivatives market.

The $1,829 support level is now critical for ETH. If buyers fail to defend it, the price could slide towards $1,725, while a recovery above $2,000 would offer some relief.

The Ethereum price is struggling to regain the $2,000 level as selling pressure continues to weigh on the broader market. Persistent outflows from spot Ethereum ETFs, reported sales from wallets linked to the Ethereum Foundation, and large whale transactions have added to concerns about investor confidence. The decline has also been accompanied by rising liquidations in the derivatives market, putting leveraged traders under pressure.

However, the sell-off is not the only story surrounding ETH. Network activity remains substantial, raising questions about the disconnect between Ethereum’s underlying usage and its recent market performance. With derivatives positioning weakening and institutional flows under scrutiny, can ETH stabilise and reclaim $2,000, or is another leg lower ahead?

Institutional withdrawals have emerged as one of the major sources of selling pressure on Ethereum. US spot Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $695.9 million in net outflows during November, with withdrawals reported in seven of the month’s first eight trading sessions. The trend continued on November 13, when the funds registered another net outflow of around $64.95 million.

Besides, on-chain activity has added to the concerns. A wallet identified by blockchain trackers as linked to the Ethereum Foundation sold another 2,000 ETH, worth approximately $3.87 million, on November 13. The wallet’s reported sales since October 26 had reached 6,785 ETH by that date. Lookonchain subsequently reported another 1,000 ETH sale on November 14, taking its tracked sales over the preceding five days to 5,000 ETH.

The #EthereumFoundation-linked wallet (0x5CBC) dumped another 1,000 $ETH($1.9M) an hour ago.Over the past 5 days, this wallet has sold 5,000 $ETH ($9.92M) at an average price of $1,983.5.https://t.co/LpNlrLUUAO pic.twitter.com/lgeVlj6AfJ

The wider whale activity is not entirely one-sided. One large holder reportedly swapped 16,700 ETH for approximately $30.94 million in USDT, while another whale accumulated 10,380 ETH, worth nearly $19.91 million, despite carrying substantial unrealised losses. These transactions point to different strategies among large holders rather than a uniform move towards selling. Still, the combination of sustained ETF withdrawals and sizeable ETH disposals has added to the market’s cautious sentiment as the token struggles below $2,000.

Ethereum’s derivatives market is showing that traders are becoming more cautious as the price struggles to recover. Open interest across exchanges has dropped to approximately $23.08 billion, down 3.85% over 24 hours. Besides, $241.41 million in ETH positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, with long positions accounting for approximately 76% of the total.

Funding rates, meanwhile, have moved close to neutral at around 0.0001%. This suggests that the earlier preference for long positions has largely faded, leaving bullish and bearish traders more evenly positioned. Futures activity remains considerably higher than spot trading, with 24-hour futures volume at approximately $47.33 billion compared with $3.10 billion in spot volume. This highlights how heavily ETH trading continues to rely on the derivatives market.

Ethereum’s daily chart continues to show signs of weakness, with the latest decline pushing ETH further below its moving averages. The bearish alignment of the EMA ribbon reflects the loss of upward momentum. A confirmed death cross, where the 50-day EMA moves below the 200-day EMA, would add another warning that the broader trend is turning increasingly bearish.

The order blocks also highlight how sellers have been gaining ground. Instead of facing resistance at one fixed level, Ethereum has encountered successive selling zones at progressively lower prices. Each recovery attempt has struggled to move through these areas, suggesting that sellers are stepping in earlier and making it harder for buyers to regain control. The latest drop below $1,900 adds to this pressure and leaves the market looking vulnerable.

Ethereum is facing pressure from multiple sides, with persistent ETF outflows, reported large-holder sales and a wave of long liquidations weighing on market sentiment. The derivatives market also shows traders scaling back their positions, while the daily chart points to a weakening price structure. The successive lower order blocks suggest that sellers are defending increasingly lower levels, making a sustained recovery more difficult.

For now, $1,829 remains the key support to watch. A breakdown below this level could expose ETH to further losses towards $1,725, while a recovery above $2,000 would be an early sign that buyers are returning. However, ETH needs to overcome the overhead selling zones and improve its broader moving-average structure before the bullish outlook can gain traction. Until then, the risk of another leg lower remains.

#5136. Binance Reveals Final Numbers After $6.34 Billion Hack: 100.04% of Shiba Inu (SHIB) Reserves Confirmed

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions.
